subject: Dedicated capacity provisioning checklist for SolarFlare (throughput, latency, headroom)
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@solarflare.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity provisioning checklist for SolarFlare (throughput, latency, headroom)

Maya / team —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As discussed, we want to align on a concrete dedicated-capacity proposal that maps SolarFlare's expected traffic to GPU slabs, plus clear headroom and fallback behavior so your SLOs are protected during spikes. Attached is a starter workbook (solarflare-dedicated-provision.xlsx) with the worksheet we'll iterate on.

High-level ask from us: can you confirm the following so we can finalize the sizing math?
- target p95 inference latency SLO (for the primary model)
- the canonical model family/size you plan to deploy (e.g., 13B dense quantized, or 6.7B low-latency variant)
- expected concurrency profile (steady TPS and peak TPS over 1/5/60m windows)
- typical prompt & response token averages (request tokens / response tokens)

Initial assumptions (please confirm or correct):
- workload: 13B quantized model (approx. 80% of answers < 256 tokens)
- steady-state peak: 350 tokens/sec aggregate in US region (burst to 1,200 tps for ~5–10m windows)
- target p95: 150–200ms end-to-end (inference only target ~120ms)

What we'll produce next:
1) tokens/sec -> GPUs mapping with per-model latencies and conservative headroom multipliers
2) suggested dedicated slab (GPU count and SKU), plus a burst policy (reserved + preemptible pool)
3) routing/fallback plan to a smaller variant for heavy bursts to maintain p95
4) canary and roll-back runbook (KV warmup guidance included)

Please attach the traffic export if handy and we'll plug it into the workbook.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachment: solarflare-dedicated-provision.xlsx

From: Maya Singh <maya@solarflare.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@solarflare.ai
Date: 2027-04-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity provisioning checklist for SolarFlare (throughput, latency, headroom)

Thanks, Kimberly — appreciate the clear checklist. Attaching our Q2 traffic export (solarflare-traffic-2027Q2.csv). Quick summary:
- model: 13B quantized (we expect to run a smaller 6B fallback only for major bursts)
- avg tokens/day: ~1.1B tokens/day
- steady TPS (business hours): 220 tokens/sec aggregate
- peak observed TPS: 1,050 tokens/sec (sustained ~6 minutes during launch cadence)
- request / response avg: 60 / 140 tokens
- SLOs: p95 end-to-end 150ms; for evaluation please assume inference-only p95 target of 110–120ms

Notes: our infra team prefers minimal cold-start variability — any guidance on KV cache warmup would be great. Also, include recommended sizing for a short warm pool (pre-warmed instances) if that materially reduces p95 tail.

Maya Singh
Head of Platform — SolarFlare AI
maya@solarflare.ai
Attachment: solarflare-traffic-2027Q2.csv

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya@solarflare.ai>
Date: 2027-04-23T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity provisioning checklist for SolarFlare (throughput, latency, headroom)

Looping in some quick math based on Maya's numbers and our runbook. See attch (gpu-mapping-math.md) for the step-by-step. Summary below.

Assumptions (conservative):
- model: 13B quantized, inference path yields ~0.9 tokens/ms on A100-v5 (quantized path; pinned to single GPU per stream when batching inefficient) => ~900 tokens/sec per GPU at low-latency config
- with batching (40–80ms batch window) we can push to ~1,800 tokens/sec on the same GPU but with p95 latency penalties; we will size for mixed-mode where 60% of requests batched, 40% low-latency single-shot
- KV cache warmup reduces p95 by ~20–30% for long-context sessions; assume 12% improvement for steady-state after warmup

Sizing calculations (rounded):
- steady TPS 220 tps * average token per request (200 tokens) => 44,000 tokens/sec aggregate; but note Maya's metric uses tokens/sec already; converting: steady-state 220 tokens/sec aggregate means my bad — using SolarFlare's stated tokens/sec: 220 tokens/sec steady, peak 1,050 tokens/sec
- GPUs needed (conservative headroom 2.0x for p95 protection without fallback):
  - steady: 220 tps / 900 tps per GPU = 0.25 GPUs -> 1 GPU for redundancy and warm pool
  - peak (1,050 tps): 1,050 / 900 = 1.17 GPUs -> 3 GPUs with 2.5x headroom to flatten variance and allow rolling updates
- But because of model size and burst characteristics, prefer a committed slab that handles predictable demand + some burst reserve: recommended committed slab = 4 x A100-v5 GPUs (covers steady + near-peak with 1.8x headroom). For high-confidence p95 120ms target, require burst buffer of 4 additional GPUs that can be pre-warmed or attached as a burst pool (total 8).

Operational notes / mitigations:
- Route low-latency traffic to a GPU pool with strict batch windows; route bulk/background work to a batching pool with higher throughput per-GPU.
- Provide a smaller 6B variant as programmatic fallback for sustained >2x peaks; transition policy in router should be time-windowed and gradual to avoid quality cliffs.
- Pre-warm policy: maintain 1–2 GPUs in a warm pool (idle but with model loaded) to cut cold-start tail; this is most valuable for unpredictable ad-hoc bursts.

I'll add the detailed math file into the shared drive. Thoughts on committed slab pricing if we choose 4x commit + burst buffer? I'll draft a pricing delta once we lock on exact GPU SKU.

Ben Carter
Sr. Solution Architect — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
Attachment: gpu-mapping-math.md

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya@solarflare.ai>
Date: 2027-04-24T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity provisioning checklist for SolarFlare (throughput, latency, headroom)

Ben — good start. A couple of asks before we lock numbers into the proposal:
1) Ben's per-GPU tps numbers look like they're for a single-stream low-latency path; can we run a quick sim that mixes 60% batched (1,800 tps/GPU) and 40% single-shot (900 tps/GPU) to compute an effective aggregate capacity and p95 projection?
2) Please include the distribution assumptions (request token lengths) we used — the workbook currently assumes 60/140 but real traffic shows a heavy tail; let's size with 90th percentile token lengths too.
3) If SolarFlare needs 110–120ms inference p95, what's the recommended headroom multiplier for resilient rolling upgrades? Ben suggested ~2x; can we validate that with a short Monte Carlo of spike shapes (sustained vs. stair-step vs. one-minute microburst)?

Operational hooks I'd like in the proposal:
- explicit canary traffic split and switchback thresholds
- fallback model thresholds (e.g., >180s sustained overcommit -> auto-fallback to 6B for a defined window)
- telemetry/alerting mapping (p95, p99, cache-warm fraction, queue-length) with runbook links

I'll kick off a 30-minute sim run this afternoon and push the results to the Drive link. Also adding the HubSpot record (see related_links).

Priyom Das
Staff SRE — Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Maya Singh <maya@solarflare.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity provisioning checklist for SolarFlare (throughput, latency, headroom)

Team / Maya —

Thanks for the quick turn. Based on Ben's conservative mapping and Priyom's asks, here's the proposal I'll present to SolarFlare in the call tomorrow:

Recommended commitment profile
- Committed slab: 4 x A100-v5 (dedicated) — covers day-to-day with ~1.8x headroom for p95 protection
- Burst pool: 4 x A100-v5 (pre-warmed) — attached automatically for sustained >1.5x steady peak for up to 15 minutes; operators can extend for a cost delta
- Fallback: 6B model variant automatically available when sustained demand >2x for longer than 2 minutes; router soft-fails by request-type to avoid universal quality cliffs

SLO mapping
- Target inference p95: 110–120ms (inference-only). With the committed slab + pre-warm policy we expect real-world p95 ~115ms with current token profile; p99 tail will be higher during microbursts but mitigated by the pre-warmed burst pool and KV cache warmup.

Action items (owners)
- Ben: run the mixed-mode sim (60% batch/40% single-shot) and produce final tokens/sec -> GPU mapping (due EOD today).
- Priyom: run the Monte Carlo spike shapes and confirm 2x headroom adequacy (deliverables to Drive).
- Lauren: draft pricing delta for 4x commit + burst buffer and update HubSpot deal SF-2027-114.
- Maya: confirm whether you want the warm pool to be billed as part of commit or as a burst add-on (this will change the contract line-item).

We'll capture the final worksheet and a short runbook for rollout/rollback in that Drive folder. If SolarFlare signs to the 4+4 model, we'll propose a 30-day canary with automatic rollback if p95 > 160ms or error rates spike >0.5%.

Kimberly Park
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com

Onward: meeting scheduled 2027-04-26 10:00 PT to review final numbers.
